items.title: Hardware report: Linux root booted from an ext4 image inside the Orbis user partition, no USB storage (Baikal Slim, 7.2 native-dev2)
items.body:
`INTERNAL-STORAGE.md` lists internal-root boot as unqualified. This is evidence from one console: two boots with the
root on the internal SSD, the second with no USB storage attached at all. It's evidence, not acceptance, and it's not an
installer. The kernel side is the existing dev2 target plus #4; everything else is initramfs/userspace.

## Console and boot chain

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Console | PS4 Slim CUH-2002A, Baikal, GPU `1002:9923`, Orbis 9.60 |
| Internal disk | Crucial CT500BX500 SATA SSD (aftermarket, not the stock HDD), `ata1`, 6.0 Gbps |
| Loader | PPPwn → GoldHEN → BinLoader → `ps4-linux-loader` v25.1 `linux-1024mb.elf` `623c3b685924…` |
| Kernel | `7.2.11-psx-ps4-baikal-native-dev2-v2icc`: target `7.2-ps4-baikal-native-dev2` at `804365c` plus the #4 patch, built locally. `bzImage` `4b1e8ca068be…`, config `c6892bf66223…` |
| Boot arguments | dev2 profile: `… pci=nocrs intremap=off ps4_bpcie.ps4_sata_phy_orbit=1 libahci.ps4_ahci_poll_ms=5 net.ifnames=0 consoleblank=0` plus `ps4root=internal`, which only the initramfs reads. No `libata.force`. |
| Initramfs | psxitarch better-initramfs `3692a4f4…` with two appended newc archives (a key hook and the internal-root step), zero-padded to 4 KiB. Boot 2: `2918d5ed89e1…`. Boot 1 used an earlier variant (`467495129afa…`) that still had the fixed `sleep 10` and a USB fallback. |
| UART | Continuous Teensy capture from before both kexecs through the end of the checks (one reconnect earlier, before either boot) |

## Layout (nothing here is a portable default)

```text
ata1 disk (found via sysfs path */ata1/*, not sdX order)
  -> Orbis user partition (partition 27 of the GPT on this console)
  -> plain dm-crypt aes-xts-plain64, 256-bit key, IV offset = (partition index 26) << 32
  -> dm-linear table over the blocks of one preallocated file, /data/linux/psxitarch.img (32 GiB)
  -> ext4 root
```

- **Key:** the loader already places the console's EAP HDD key in the initramfs as `/key/eap_hdd_key.bin`. The key never
  leaves the console. It's not in the archive, a log or this report.
- **The image** was created from Orbis over GoldHEN FTP (zeros, 32 GiB), so Orbis's own filesystem code did the allocation.
- **Block map:** built once from a full Linux boot on USB, with the crypt mapping and UFS2 mounted **read-only**. FIBMAP on
  the image (4 KiB blocks) gave 1100 extents, 67108864 sectors, no holes. Before any write, I mapped the table read-only
  and compared it with `/dev/zero` (all 32 GiB identical), which shows every mapped block belongs to the zero-filled file.
- **Linux never mounts Orbis's UFS2 read-write.** Writes go only to the image's blocks through dm-linear, so Linux's UFS2
  write path is never used. The trade-off: the table is fixed, so the file must never be deleted, moved or rewritten from
  Orbis. If it were, the next boot would write ext4 over whatever Orbis put there. The initramfs checks the UFS2 superblock
  magic and the ext4 UUID before mounting, but that only catches gross mistakes.
- **Initramfs step** (only with `ps4root=internal`): wait up to 20 s for the ata1 disk, open the crypt mapping, check the
  magic, `dmsetup create` the table (dynamic `dmsetup` plus libs copied in, `DM_DISABLE_UDEV=1`), check the UUID, mount
  ext4 read-write. On any failure it removes what it set up. It then logs `ps4-internal-root: FAILED` and starts the
  better-initramfs rescue shell, with no fallback to USB.
- **Boot files without USB:** with no USB FAT present, the loader reads `bzImage`, `initramfs.cpio.gz` and `bootargs.txt`
  from Orbis `/data/linux/boot/`. Its strings list `/mnt/usb0`, `/mnt/usb1`, `/data/linux/boot`, `/user/system/boot`; I
  think that's the search order, but I only tested the USB → `/data` case.
- In the USB-root system, a udev rule keeps every internal partition read-only. On an internal-root boot it exempts only
  the disk node and partition 27.

## Results

**EXP-20261031-012: PASS (2 boots, 1 power-off, 1 Orbis check). Not endurance-tested.**

| Boot | Boot files from | Root mounted | `systemd-analyze` | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | USB FAT | 24.7 s | 41.6 s | old init with the fixed `sleep 10`; USB root present but not mounted |
| 2 | Orbis `/data/linux/boot`, **no USB storage attached** | 14.7 s | 31.3 s | sleep removed for the internal path |

- UART excerpt (boot 2):
  ```
  [    5.997069] ata1: SATA link up 6.0 Gbps (SStatus 133 SControl 300)
  [   11.483096] Run /init as init process
  [   14.717442] EXT4-fs (dm-1): mounted filesystem <uuid> r/w with ordered data mode. Quota mode: disabled.
  [   14.730236] ps4-internal-root: root is the internal image (UUID <uuid>)
  ```
- `findmnt /` = `/dev/mapper/ps4root ext4 rw`. `systemctl is-system-running` = `running`, no failed units. No ATA, EXT4 or
  I/O errors in dmesg on either boot.
- **I/O on boot 1:** 1 GiB of random data written with `conv=fsync` at 253 MB/s, then caches dropped and read back with a
  matching sha256. A raw `dd iflag=direct` read of the mapping ran at 306 MB/s. Short tests only; no sustained, random or
  error-path I/O.
- **Power-off from the internal root (boot 1), with the #4 kernel:** `EXT4-fs (dm-1): re-mounted … ro`, "All filesystems
  unmounted", then systemd-shutdown reports `Could not detach DM /dev/dm-0: Device or resource busy` (expected: the root
  sits on it and there's no shutdown initramfs), syncs, `reboot: Power down`. The console turned fully off.
- **Orbis afterwards:** booted normally. UART shows `nmount_ufs … to /eap_user OK` and `nmount /data to /user/data OK`, with
  no UFS errors, and no database-rebuild prompt on screen. That's one check, not a long-term claim about Orbis's filesystem.

## Not tested

Repeated cold boots beyond these two, long uptime, heavy or random I/O, power loss during writes, the stock HDD, other
consoles or firmware, Aeolia/Belize, growing the image, Orbis updates or database rebuilds after the image exists, and a
power-off from boot 2.

items.title: feat: merge dev — FTP module, Rest Mode recovery, FPS overlay, plugin manager
items.body:
> Migrated from GitHub PR [#26](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN/pull/26)
> Author: `aydencharles` · Created: `2026-08-22T15:20:57Z` · State: `closed`
> Pull request `aydencharles:dev` → `aydencharles:main` · merged=`True` · merge_commit=`864f374a6c5039d9aedb61be5b96623819ebdd87`
## What

Merge the current `dev` branch into `main`: remove embedded ShadowMountPlus, turn FTP into an in-process util module with configurable port, add FPS to the overlay, improve Rest Mode recovery (toolbox/IPC/FTP), add a built-in plugin manager, harden payload process handling, and include the related cheats, shellui, logging, and docs updates.

## Why

`main` still ships the older embedded FTP/ShadowMountPlus startup path and weaker Rest Mode recovery. `dev` has the current architecture and the accumulated fixes/features from the last several days; merging it brings `main` in line with the actively developed stack.

## Checklist

- [x] Change stays on this request
- [x] `make -C source/util/tests test` passes
- [x] `docs/arch.md` updated if modules, IPC, paths, or dependencies changed
- [x] i18n keys updated in every locale if user-facing text changed

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added a built-in FTP server with configurable startup behavior and port settings.
  * Added Remote Play pairing with PIN display, account validation, and pairing status notifications.
  * Added online cheat catalog synchronization with mirror selection, progress tracking, cancellation, and process/hash-aware cheat files.
  * Added an optional in-game FPS overlay with live measurements.
  * Improved payload autostart and duplicate-launch handling.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved recovery after standby, listener failures, and service interruptions.
  * Added dedicated crash-log capture and clearer crash-report guidance.
* **Documentation**
  * Expanded setup, configuration, Docker build, FTP, Remote Play, payload, and cheat synchronization documentation.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
